title: L8 — WHO IS THE HOUSE?
voice: Sometimes the person betting against your trade is the same company that took your money to place it. You'll never see it happen. But when you lose, they win — directly. Here's how to tell whose side you're really on.
Sometimes your order goes out to the real market, and matches with another trader who wanted the opposite. Fair. Neutral. Your broker just carries the message and takes a small cut for the trip.

But sometimes the order never leaves the building. Your broker takes the other side themselves. You want to buy — they sell to you, from their own book. Now you have a position. And so do they. The exact opposite of yours.

Look at what that means. If your broker holds the opposite of your trade, then your loss is their gain. When you lose, they win — directly. Not a fee. The whole amount. Your bad trade becomes their good one.

This isn't illegal, and it isn't always bad — it's a business model. But it's one you should know you're inside. When the house can take the other side of your bet, ask one question before you trust the table: who profits when I lose?

_rules.doctrine: B-book presente comme MODELE, pas comme arnaque ('this isn't illegal, it's a business model'). Mecanique du conflit d'interet, jamais accusation nominative. Pas de nom de broker.
_rules.fusil: une fleche d'ordre (S1) dont la destination — marche neutre (S2) ou broker contrepartie (S3) — decide si ta perte enrichit quelqu'un (S4), revelee en deux destinations (S5).
_rules.figures: broker + autre trader = fil-de-fer. toi = boule teal, jamais une figure.
_rules.interdits: pas de chiffre; le broker n'est pas 'brun' (pas un mechant — une structure); pas de nom de broker; bas du cadre vide.
_rules.hook_v1_archived: You click buy. Somewhere, instantly, someone takes the other side. You never see them. You never ask who. But that question — who sold to you — decides more than you think.
_rules.hook_v2_veille: payoff <3s, framing negatif/contre-intuitif, curiosity gap (lois veille concurrente juillet 2026). Doctrine gardee: aucun mensonge, BEE.

caption:
When you click buy, someone takes the other side. Sometimes it's another trader. Sometimes it's the house.

If your broker holds the opposite of your trade, your loss becomes their gain — directly. Not a fee. The whole amount. This isn't illegal. But you should know you're inside it.

Comment "LINE" for the series on how trading actually works.
